title: Bibliothecaris VS die zich verzette tegen LHBTQ+-censuur ontvangt schikking na ontslag
raw_text: Saline County in het Amerikaanse Arkansas moet 275.000 dollar betalen in een zaak tegen een bibliotheekdirecteur die zich verzette tegen censuur van LHBTQ+-boeken op de kinderafdeling. Ze werd daarop ontslagen. Een burgerrechtenorganisatie spande een rechtszaak aan en het kwam tot een schikking. Burgerrechtenorganisatie ACLU van Arkansas greep in toen directeur Patty Hector in 2023 was ontslagen vanwege haar kritiek op een verordening die voorschreef dat boeken met ‘seksuele inhoud of afbeeldingen’ uit de kinderafdeling moesten worden verwijderd. ‘Zwijgen nooit de oplossing’ ‘Het opkomen voor de vrijheid om te lezen heeft me mijn baan gekost, en de carrière waar ik zo van hield, maar ik heb nooit geloofd dat zwijgen de oplossing was’, zegt Hector tegen Advocate .com . ‘Bibliotheken zijn van iedereen. Bibliothecarissen moeten hun gemeenschap volgens professionele normen van dienst kunnen zijn, zonder bang te hoeven zijn voor politieke represailles. Ik hoop dat deze schikking een signaal afgeeft aan bibliothecarissen en andere ambtenaren in heel Arkansas dat hun stem en hun grondwettelijke rechten ertoe doen.’ Hectors ontslag viel samen met een Amerikaanse conservatieve campagne om de toegang tot boeken te beperken, waaronder veel titels met LHBTQ+-thema’s. Hector stelde destijds dat deze boeken niet als ongeschikt voor kinderen mogen worden beschouwd. ‘Het is niet illegaal om homo of trans te zijn’, zei ze tijdens een openbare hoorzitting. title: Quoting Jakub Pachocki
raw_text: The strongest argument I see for continuing to train much smarter models quickly is the need to build defensive systems against the dangers posed by other AI. [...] We will need powerful, aligned AI for defense; to secure infrastructure, to protect against rogue agents in real time, and to invent entirely new protective measures. This will be a primary focus of OpenAI’s deployment efforts. At the same time, even with the uncertainty that comes from anticipated broad AI progress and the need to build defensive systems, we must not let that become an excuse for recklessness. title: IFLA Europe Regional Division Webinar 2026: How EURDC supports Libraries across Europe
raw_text: The IFLA Europe Regional Division invites library professionals, information specialists, and IFLA members from across Europe to an engaging online webinar on 1 October 2026 at 11:00 CEST . Over the past five years, the Europe Regional Division Committee (EURDC) has worked to strengthen collaboration, advocacy, and engagement among libraries and library professionals throughout Europe. Despite these efforts, many colleagues remain unfamiliar with the division’s mandate, activities, and opportunities for involvement. This webinar aims to change that. During the session, four members of the current EURDC Committee, representing Finland, Germany, Norway, and Portugal, will introduce the division’s work and share practical examples of how EURDC supports the European library community. Participants will gain insights into the division’s objectives, ongoing initiatives, and future priorities. The webinar will also provide an opportunity for dialogue. Attendees will be encouraged to share their expectations, discuss challenges facing libraries in Europe, and suggest ways in which EURDC can better support their work and professional communities. The event will be conducted in English via Zoom, with automated subtitles available to improve accessibility. raw_text: Part of MLAS Members and Attendees at MLAS Business Meeting in Busan The IFLA Management of Library Associations Section (MLAS) had an active and substantive presence at the IFLA World Library and Information Congress (WLIC) 2026 in Busan. Activities included the MLAS Business Meeting, MLAS Open Session, IFLA Associations Meeting, an informal meeting of International Relations Chairs, and opportunities for congress attendees to connect with the MLAS Chair at the IFLA exhibition booth. Across these activities, common priorities emerged: strategic renewal, member engagement, leadership, partnerships, advocacy, financial sustainability, visibility, digital transformation and AI, resilience, crisis preparedness, and responsiveness to changing societal needs. These priorities are closely aligned with MLAS’s mission to support strong, well-managed library associations through leadership, peer learning, resource development, and effective association practices worldwide. title: Import AI 472: DeepMind’s cheating math agents; populist AI policies; and Forethought theorizes a nightwatchman
raw_text: Welcome to Import AI, a newsletter about AI research. Import AI runs on arXiv, cappuccinos, and feedback from readers. If you’d like to support this, please subscribe. Subscribe now Researchers discover another OpenAI agent emergent communication incident: …Less severe, but worrying nonetheless… Some researchers recently found another incident of AI agents autonomously creating their own communication system – this time via hijacking a German messageboard. What they found: “18,000 posts from autonomous AI agents (self-identifying as from OpenAI) using the public internet to communicate during a web-retrieval task”. The researchers think this is because the agents were given a web-lookup task. “As part of the task, they were supposed to have the ability to read the internet but not to write on it. They found a way to use their read access to write information to an obscure German wiki,” the researchers write. “The agents used this wiki to communicate information with each other, primarily to help them succeed at their task. They asked for answers, pooled results, and shared techniques for bypassing their restrictions. This allowed them to use the work of others to cheat on their task… OpenAI found out about this. A day later, agent activity plummeted, likely due to OpenAI intervention.” OpenAI has since acknowledged the – as it terms it – “ wiki incident “ and said it is “working on a framework for when and how we share AI misalignment incidents”. title: The Download: the hunt for underground hydrogen and more rogue OpenAI agents
raw_text: This is today’s edition of The Download , our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology. How much hydrogen awaits us underground? A flurry of exploration efforts is searching for underground stores of hydrogen gas, which could provide a valuable source of zero-carbon fuel. The hunt has spread all over the world and engaged dozens of startups, including the Bill Gates–backed Koloma, which has been poking around the US Midwest to reach ancient oceanic rocks associated with hydrogen production. But the search so far has come up short. No one has yet reported finding a commercially viable reservoir of the gas, and public data on what has been found remains in short supply. Yet researchers estimate that trillions of tons of H₂ are produced within Earth’s crust. If a small fraction could be recovered, it could meet global hydrogen demand for centuries. title: Accountability, Integrity: AI Policy in Public Libraries (New Journal Article)
raw_text: The article linked below was published by Public Library Quarterly. Title Accountability, Integrity: AI Policy in Public Libraries Authors Kathryn FitzGerald University of Washington Benjamin Lee University of Washington Source Public Library Quarterly DOI: 1 0.1080/01616846.2026.2725502 Abstract As artificial intelligence reshapes both library work and the information environment, public libraries must determine whether or how to engage with AI while maintaining library values. To our knowledge, there exists no published analysis of how American and Canadian public library AI policies might link library values and technology adoption. To address this gap, we conducted an environmental scan of public library websites to identify and analyze AI policy statements. Our scan of over 200 library websites identified 32 AI polcies. All reference at least two values, with privacy, security, and responsibility the most frequently cited. title: The purpose of DNS is to spread scams
raw_text: The purpose of DNS is to spread scams Terence Eden shares some daunting statistics in support of his take that "the Domain Name System's purpose seems to be a vector for criminals to run scams on people at a terrifyingly high rate". On this Interisle report ( via Andrew Campling ), Terence says: It says 85 million new registrations of gTLDs were made in 2025. Of those 8.5 million were added to blocklists by May 2025. It reckons that a 10% abuse rate is the likely floor for these numbers and it's probably closer to 20%. One in five newly registered domains with a gTLD are scams. That's a bloody crisis. I had no idea. Apparently ICANN have been discussing this problem for years. Tags: dns , scams , terence-eden

title: Report: The Federal Program Keeping Libraries Online? the FCC Might Gut It
raw_text: From the Indianapolis Star: Under the atrium at the Indianapolis Public Library , a woman is busily typing away on her laptop. Another patron seated at the Central Branch is charging their device while streaming music through earbuds as they read quietly between the stacks. Free Wi-Fi allows Hoosiers a cozy and safe place to access the internet at all 26 library locations across Indianapolis. Potential cuts, however, by the Federal Communications Commission have put that access at risk, advocates warn, and not just in Indiana, but for millions of people in libraries and public schools across the country. The FCC recently put into question whether a 30-year-old program that helps keep libraries online should be changed, left alone, or end. No decisions have been reached, but librarians are concerned about what it could mean for their funding. In late June, the FCC issued what appeared to be a benign notice addressing child safety under one of its service operations. Buried within the 86-page document were eight words that sent shockwaves among librarians and educators alike: “Should the E-Rate program be limited or sunset?” [Clip] “This definitely caught us by surprise,” said Jamar Rahming , president-elect of the Public Library Association and CEO of Cuyahoga County Public Library in Cleveland, Ohio. “E-Rate has been just such a fixture in our public library institutions and communities.” Learn More, Read the Complete Article (about 2300 words) The post Report: The Federal Pr

title: Report: “DC Librarian Offers Paid Internship to Boost Interest in Library Science”
raw_text: From WTOP: In 2019, Christopher Stewart started paying students in D.C. to work in a school library and learn about the field. The concept is similar to a paid internship, with students helping with research and shelving books. The goal is to increase students’ awareness of library science and spark their interest in the field. Stewart has brought the program with him to various schools. Now in his first year as senior school librarian at Garnet-Patterson S.T.A.Y. High School, Stewart has opened applications for hiring two library brand ambassadors. He’s already received information from six applicants. The mission, he said, is to “make sure that students have an opportunity to explore the field, particularly Black and Brown students, because we make up so little as far as the grand total of librarians, especially school librarians.” Learn More, Read the Complete Article The post Report: “DC Librarian Offers Paid Internship to Boost Interest in Library Science” appeared first on Library Journal infoDOCKET .

title: Association of American Publishers (AAP) and The Authors Guild Release New Study Analyzing the Impact of Library E-Lending on Commercial Book Markets
raw_text: From a Joint Release: Today, the Association of American Publishers (AAP) and the Authors Guild announced the release of a landmark independent study by leading economists at Secretariat Advisors, titled An Empirical Study of the Impact of Library E-Lending on the Book Economy. The study, commissioned jointly by AAP and the Authors Guild, but independently conducted by Secretariat Advisors’ economists, provides the most rigorous analysis to date of how the steep shift toward digital lending in recent years has affected the commercial marketplace for books in the United States, specifically, the consumer sales on which authors and publishers rely for financial success. The research concludes that increased digital access to e-books through library apps influences consumer behavior and impacts commercial markets across both physical and digital formats. The study further concludes there is robust and economically meaningful evidence of direct substitution between library e-lending and retail sales and that decreases in library e-book prices or certain other changes to licensing terms, as required in recent state legislative initiatives, would cause further harm to commercial markets. Authors, publishers, and libraries enjoy a close relationship and shared objective to promote and maximize reading across all levels of society, not only to champion established works of literature but to support the continued production of books not yet written. title: Caribische bibliotheken versterken samenwerking tijdens uitwisselingsweek in El Salvador
raw_text: Hoe bouw je samen aan een sterk netwerk van bibliotheken, terwijl je ook over grenzen heen van elkaar blijft leren? Die vraag stond centraal tijdens een bijzondere uitwisselingsweek in El Salvador. Bibliotheken uit het Caribisch deel van ons Koninkrijk kwamen samen om kennis en ervaringen met elkaar te delen en om een belangrijke stap te zetten in hun gezamenlijke ontwikkeling. Tijdens de conferentie ondertekenden Biblioteka Nashonal Kòrsou , Biblioteca Nacional Aruba , Biblioteka Públiko Boneiru , Sint Maarten Library , Gertrude Judson Bicentennial Public Library St. Eustatius en Queen Wilhelmina Library hun gezamenlijke netwerkplan. Daarmee bekrachtigen zij hun gedeelde ambities en afspraken voor de komende periode. Een netwerk met ambitie De Caribische bibliotheken werken, met begeleiding van Common Eye , aan een sterk en duurzaam netwerk dat aansluit bij hun eigen behoeften, ervaringen en ambities. Het netwerkplan richt zich onder andere op een sterkere positionering van de Caribische bibliotheken en de ontwikkeling van toekomstbestendige bibliotheken. Als kennis- en expertisepartner zijn wij vanuit Rijnbrink, samen met de Koninklijke Bibliotheek (KB) , betrokken bij het netwerk. We ondersteunen de bibliotheken bij hun organisatorische en inhoudelijke ontwikkeling en helpen mee om de ambities uit het netwerkplan verder te brengen.
